title: TORQUE: Optimizing What (not) to Quantize Before and After Rotation
abstract: arXiv:2609.36032v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Uniform random rotations are an effective preprocessing step for quantization: they make normalized coordinate distributions approximately Gaussian, enabling the use of codebooks optimized offline. We introduce TORQUE, a framework that improves on previous quantization works that use random rotations by jointly optimizing how many and which coordinates to preserve at high precision both before and after rotation, under a fixed overall expected bit budget.   Intuitively, before rotation, preserving large input coordinates at high precision can reduce overall error by preventing the rotation from spreading their values across many coordinates. Likewise, after rotation, preserving a small fraction of the largest-magnitude coordinates at high precision allows the remaining values to be quantized more accurately using codebooks optimized offline for the resulting truncated Gaussian distribution.   We derive a quantization error upper bound

translated_title: TORQUE：在旋转前后优化哪些内容该量化与不该量化
translated_abstract: 均匀随机旋转是量化的一种有效预处理步骤：它能使归一化后的坐标分布近似为高斯分布，从而可以使用离线优化的码本。我们提出了TORQUE，这是一个对以往使用随机旋转的量化工作的改进框架，它在固定的整体期望比特预算下，联合优化在旋转之前和之后应分别以高精度保留多少个以及哪些坐标。直观地说，在旋转之前，以高精度保留较大的输入坐标可以防止旋转将这些值分散到多个坐标中，从而降低整体误差。同样，在旋转之后，以高精度保留一小部分幅值最大的坐标，可以使用针对所得截断高斯分布离线优化的码本，对其余值进行更准确的量化。我们推导出了量化误差的上界……
tldr: TORQUE是一个在固定比特预算下，联合优化旋转前后应保留哪些高精度坐标的量化框架，可显著降低整体量化误差。
en_tdlr: TORQUE is a quantization framework that jointly optimizes which coordinates to preserve at high precision before and after random rotations under a fixed bit budget, effectively reducing overall quantization error.
